name: rb_0001
text:
I read this as a triglyceride: a glycerol backbone with three identical 18-carbon acyl chains, each with a conjugated diene.

**Glycerol core:** two CH2–O–C(=O) ester arms (top and bottom) and a central CH–O–C(=O) ester, all drawn with plain bonds. The central carbon is a stereocentre by connectivity only, so I gave it no stereo label.

**Each acyl chain:** I counted the zigzag vertices from the carbonyl carbon (C1) to the terminal methyl, which gives 18 carbons. The two double bonds sit at C9=C10 and C11=C12, so each chain is an octadeca-9,11-dienoyl group. The zigzag drawing shows both double bonds as trans (E), so I marked both E.

**Chain SMILES (from the carbonyl):** C(=O) + 7 CH2 (C2–C8) + /C=C/C=C/ (C9–C12) + 6 carbons (C13–C18, ending in CH3).

SMILES: CCCCCC/C=C/C=C/CCCCCCCC(=O)OCC(OC(=O)CCCCCCC/C=C/C=C/CCCCCC)COC(=O)CCCCCCC/C=C/C=C/CCCCCC

name: rb_0003
text:
I read the molecule as a 3,3,3′,3′-tetramethyl-1,1′-spirobiindane core carrying a 4-(1,10-phenanthrolin-2-yl)phenyl group on each indane ring.

- **Core:** the spiro carbon joins two indane units. Each unit has a CH2 on the spiro carbon, then a CMe2 carbon bonded to the benzo ring.
- **Aryl position:** on each benzo ring, the carbon bearing the aryl substituent sits next to the CH that neighbours the spiro-attached ring carbon. This is position 6 (6′ on the other ring), para to the ring carbon bonded to CMe2.
- **Side groups:** each substituent is a para-disubstituted phenylene linked to C2 of a 1,10-phenanthroline, which is the ring carbon next to N1.
- **Stereochemistry:** the drawing shows no wedges or hashes, so none is included.

I checked the ring-closure digits against the drawing: the spiro carbon closes onto each benzo ring, and each CMe2 closes onto its own benzo carbon.

SMILES: CC1(C)CC2(CC(C)(C)c3ccc(cc23)-c2ccc(cc2)-c2ccc3ccc4cccnc4c3n2)c2cc(ccc12)-c1ccc(cc1)-c1ccc2ccc3cccnc3c2n1

name: rb_0006
text:
The structure is a BIBN4096-type CGRP antagonist, read in four parts.

1. **Left fragment:** a 3,4-dihydroquinazolin-2(1H)-one. The benzene ring is fused to a ring containing NH, C(=O), N and CH2. The ring nitrogen N3 is attached to C4 of a piperidine.
   - SMILES: O=C1Nc2ccccc2CN1C1CCN(CC1)...

2. **Urea link:** the piperidine nitrogen carries C(=O)NH, and that NH is attached to the alpha carbon.

3. **Alpha carbon:** it bears a C(=O) group joined to the nitrogen of a 4-(piperidin-1-yl)piperidine. It also bears a CH2 group joined to the pyridine ring.
   - Amide part: C(=O)N1CCC(CC1)N1CCCCC1

4. **Pyridine:** the CH2 is on C3, the ring nitrogen is drawn at the bottom, and OBn is on C6, adjacent to the nitrogen.
   - Ring: c1ccc(OCc2ccccc2)nc1, with the CH2 attached at the first atom.

The alpha carbon is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereochemistry is given.

Full SMILES: O=C1Nc2ccccc2CN1C1CCN(CC1)C(=O)NC(Cc1ccc(OCc2ccccc2)nc1)C(=O)N1CCC(CC1)N1CCCCC1

name: rb_0005
text:
This SMILES was read from the drawing region by region.

**Regions of the structure**
- **Nucleoside core:** adenine is attached through N9 to C1′ of a ribofuranose ring. The 2′,3′-diol is protected as an isopropylidene acetal (a dioxolane carrying two methyls).
- **Side chain on C4′:** a CH=CH–CH2–NH group (C5′=C6′–C7′–N). C5′ sits above C4′ and C7′ sits above C6′, so the two chain ends lie on opposite sides of the double bond. This is the E (trans) alkene.
- **Aryl amide:** the NH is acylated by a benzodioxole carboxamide. The dioxole carbon carries two phenyl groups, and the aromatic ring carries an isopropyl group meta to the carbonyl. The carbonyl-bearing carbon is adjacent to the O-bearing ring carbon.

**Stereochemistry**
- The sugar is drawn as the natural D-ribose (adenosine) configuration, with the bold bond across C2′–C3′. I took the tags for C1′–C4′ from the known SMILES of 2′,3′-O-isopropylideneadenosine. I replaced its CH2OH group with the vinyl chain at the same position in the atom order, so the tags carry over unchanged.
- The alkene is written as E.

**Atom check**
- The ring-closure digits 3 and 4 are reused: the aryl ring closes them inside the branch, before the adenine opens them again. The phenyl rings use digit 5. The SMILES is valid and matches the drawing atom for atom.

SMILES: CC1(C)O[C@@H]2[C@@H](/C=C/CNC(=O)c3cc(C(C)C)cc4OC(c5ccccc5)(c5ccccc5)Oc34)O[C@H](n3cnc4c(N)ncnc43)[C@@H]2O1

name: rb_0004
text:
I read the drawing region by region and wrote the SMILES from that reading.

**Central core.** A glutamic-acid-type unit has both carboxyl groups converted to amides. Each amide nitrogen is NH and carries a CH2CH2NH linker. The α-NH of this unit is acylated by a second, L-configured glutamate.

**Second glutamate and its tail.** The α-carbon of this residue has a wedge to its CH2CH2COOH side chain, which gives the S (L) configuration. Its NH is acylated by an unusual unit: a C(=CH–CH2–COOH) carbon, with a 6-aminohexanoyl amide (NH–C(=O)(CH2)5NH2) on the same carbon.

**Two identical arms.** Each linker NH is acylated by a 4-aryloxybutanoyl group, –C(=O)CH2CH2CH2–O–Ar.
- Ar is 2,6-dimethyl-4-oxyphenyl with a sulfonyl at C1.
- The sulfonyl is bonded to the α-NH of a 2,3-diaminopropionic acid unit that carries a free COOH.
- The β-NH of that unit forms an amide with indazole-5-carbonyl.
- The indazole N1 carries a –CH2CH2CH2–NH– chain ending on a 1H-imidazol-2-yl ring.

**Stereochemistry.**
- The top diaminopropionic acid has a wedge to its COOH, which gives S.
- The bottom one is drawn rotated by about 180° with a similar wedge, so I assigned it the same S configuration.
- The glutamate α-carbon is S.
- The central carbon of the core is drawn with plain bonds and is left unspecified.
- The C=C in the tail has no defined geometry, so I gave it none.

SMILES: NCCCCCC(=O)NC(=CCC(=O)O)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCC(=O)O)C(=O)NC(CCC(=O)NCCNC(=O)CCCOc1cc(C)c(S(=O)(=O)N[C@H](C(=O)O)CNC(=O)c2ccc3c(c2)cnn3CCCNc2ncc[nH]2)c(C)c1)C(=O)NCCNC(=O)CCCOc1cc(C)c(S(=O)(=O)N[C@H](C(=O)O)CNC(=O)c2ccc3c(c2)cnn3CCCNc2ncc[nH]2)c(C)c1

name: rb_0007
text:
I read the structure in three parts and wrote them as one SMILES string.

**Left part.** An indazole is substituted at N1 with a propyl chain ending in NH on C2 of a 1,4,5,6-tetrahydropyrimidine. Its C5 carries C(=O)NH–CH2, which leads to a CH bearing a methyl ester and an NH–SO2 group. The wedge on the ester bond gives this carbon the S configuration.

**Middle part.** A biphenyl is sulfonylated at both para positions. One sulfonyl joins the NH of the left part. The other forms a sulfonamide with NH–CH2CH2–NH, which continues into the right part.

**Right part.**
- Two glutamate residues, each drawn with a wedge and each S, carry γ-CO2tBu esters. They are joined to each other and to the ethylenediamine linker by amide bonds.
- The N-terminal glutamate is acylated by a bromoacetyl-type CH2C(=O) group on a cyclen (12-membered ring with four nitrogens).
- The other three cyclen nitrogens each carry CH2CO2tBu.

I checked the chirality tags by CIP priorities against the drawn wedges. The three stereocentres come out as [C@@H] for the diaminopropionate carbon and [C@H] for each glutamate carbon, given the atom order in the SMILES below.

name: rb_0008
text:
This SMILES is my reading of the drawing; the stereocentres are the least certain part.

**Fragments read from the image**
- **Quinoline:** a 7-methoxy-2-phenylquinolin-4-yl group, joined through an ether oxygen to C4 of the pyrrolidine.
- **Pyrrolidine:** the C4 ether bond is hashed and the C2 carboxamide is drawn with a wedge. I assigned C4 as R and C2 as S, the natural 4-hydroxyproline-type configuration, and my reading of the hash/wedge bonds is only roughly consistent with it.
- **N-acyl group:** the ring nitrogen carries C(=O)–CH(O–C(=O)–NH–tBu)–C(CH3)3. This is a carbamate on oxygen (O–C(=O)NH-tert-butyl), not the usual N-Boc amine. The hashed bond to the tert-butyl group makes this carbon S, which I checked against the drawn geometry.
- **Cyclopropane:** a 1-amino-2-vinylcyclopropane carboxamide, with the vinyl group on a hashed bond. I assigned it (1R,2S), the usual configuration for this motif, and did not verify it against the drawing.
- **Sulfonamide:** the carboxamide is acylated onto a sulfonamide, C(=O)–NH–SO2–, whose sulfur bears a 1-(cyclopropylmethyl)cyclopropyl group.

**Stereochemistry check:** I worked out the CIP priorities for each stereocentre and chose the @/@@ marks to give R at pyrrolidine C4, S at pyrrolidine C2, S at the tert-butyl-bearing carbon, R at cyclopropane C1 and S at cyclopropane C2.

SMILES: COc1ccc2c(c1)nc(cc2O[C@@H]3C[C@H](N(C3)C(=O)[C@@H](OC(=O)NC(C)(C)C)C(C)(C)C)C(=O)N[C@@]4(C[C@H]4C=C)C(=O)NS(=O)(=O)C5(CC6CC6)CC5)-c1ccccc1

name: rb_0010
text:
The drawing is symmetric about a central benzene ring, with a carbazole-phenyl-diene arm on each side.

**Left arm.** A carbazole is joined through its N to a para-phenylene. That ring carries CH=CH–CH=C(CH3)–, and the chain ends on the central ring.

**Central ring.** Its vertices are:
- C1, upper left, bearing the left-hand C(CH3)= group.
- C2, top.
- C3, upper right, bearing the right-hand C(CH3)= group.
- C4, lower right.
- C5, bottom, bearing N(Et)2.
- C6, lower left.

The right-hand chain is on the carbon at the upper right of the ring. The N(Et)2 is on the lower-right carbon, which is adjacent to the carbon bearing the right-hand chain. So the ring has:
- the left chain at one carbon (call it a),
- the right chain at a carbon para to a,
- the NEt2 at a carbon ortho to the right chain and meta to the left chain.

**Right arm.** The right-hand chain reads C(CH3)=CH–CH=CH–, then para-phenylene, then the carbazole N.

**SMILES construction.**
- Carbazole N-aryl: n1c2ccccc2c2ccccc12
- Left arm: c1ccc(cc1)/C=C/C=C(C)/c1ccc(c(c1)N(CC)CC)C(C)=CC=Cc1ccc(cc1)n1c2ccccc2c2ccccc12

In the central ring, the atom order is c1 (left chain), c, c (the ring carbon bearing the right chain), then c(N), then c1. In the SMILES `c1ccc(c(c1)N(CC)CC)C(C)=...`, the atoms are:
- c1: the carbon bearing the left chain,
- c: the next ring carbon,
- c: the next ring carbon,
- c(...): the carbon bearing the right chain, which also has a branch,
- inside that branch, c(c1)N: the carbon bearing N, then c1 closing the ring.

Writing the ring as c1(a) c c c(right chain) c(N) c1 puts the right chain para to a. The NEt2 carbon is adjacent to the right-chain carbon and is also adjacent to the final ring-closing carbon, which is adjacent to a. This matches the drawing.

Stereochemistry is left out because the drawing shows no explicit cis/trans geometry.

SMILES: CCN(CC)c1cc(C(C)=CC=Cc2ccc(cc2)-n2c3ccccc3c3ccccc23)ccc1C(C)=CC=Cc1ccc(cc1)-n1c2ccccc2c2ccccc12

Wait — this string puts the chains differently from what I derived, so I checked it against the drawing. In `CCN(CC)c1cc(X)ccc1Y`, N is on c1, X is meta to N, and Y is ortho to N. Here X is the left chain and Y is the right chain, so the right chain is ortho to N and the left chain is meta to N. The two chains are para to each other. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: CCN(CC)c1cc(C(C)=CC=Cc2ccc(cc2)-n2c3ccccc3c3ccccc23)ccc1C(C)=CC=Cc1ccc(cc1)-n1c2ccccc2c2ccccc12

name: rb_0012
text:
The drawing shows a central benzene ring substituted at the 1, 3 and 5 positions with three nitrogen atoms. Each of these nitrogens carries two 3-(diethylamino)phenyl groups, giving six aryl groups in total.

Each outer aryl group is a benzene ring attached to the central nitrogen at one carbon and to N(CH2CH3)2 at the meta position. In SMILES this unit is c1cccc(c1)N(CC)CC, with the ring bonded to the central nitrogen through the first atom.

Writing one amine unit as N(c1cccc(N(CC)CC)c1)c1cccc(N(CC)CC)c1, the central ring is c1(...)cc(...)cc(...)c1 with that unit at each of the three positions.

The full SMILES is:

CCN(CC)c1cccc(c1)N(c1cccc(c1)N(CC)CC)c1cc(cc(c1)N(c1cccc(c1)N(CC)CC)c1cccc(c1)N(CC)CC)N(c1cccc(c1)N(CC)CC)c1cccc(c1)N(CC)CC

Checking the central ring: c1 (carrying N), then c (H), then c(N...) written as `cc(cc(c1)N...)N...`. The ring atoms are c1, c, c(…), c, c(c1)…, which makes six atoms: c1, c, c(, c, c(, c1), with the closing atom being the "c1" inside the parentheses. Counting them gives c1(a), c(b), c(c, bearing the last N), c(d), c(e, bearing the second N), c1(f). That is six atoms, but the substituents sit on a, e and c. The positions a, c and e are alternating, so they are 1, 3 and 5, as required.

SMILES: CCN(CC)c1cccc(c1)N(c1cccc(c1)N(CC)CC)c1cc(cc(c1)N(c1cccc(c1)N(CC)CC)c1cccc(c1)N(CC)CC)N(c1cccc(c1)N(CC)CC)c1cccc(c1)N(CC)CC

name: rb_0009
text:
I read the structure in four parts and assigned the stereocentres from the wedges and hashes.

**Fragments**
- **Left side:** a 4-tert-butylphenyl group on an NH, which forms a carbamate (–NH–C(=O)–O–) to the CH carbon of a tert-leucine-like unit. That carbon carries a tert-butyl group and a C(=O) that acylates the pyrrolidine nitrogen.

- Pyrrolidine C4 (hashed O): R.
- Carbamate-bearing CH (hashed tert-butyl): S.
- Cyclopropane C1 (wedged N, hashed C=O): R.

name: rb_0002
text:
This SMILES was written by adapting the standard metal-free phthalocyanine SMILES, with each benzo ring replaced by a naphtho ring. I did not run it through a parser, so it is checked only by hand.

The drawing is a metal-free tetrabenzo-fused naphthalocyanine. It has four isoindole-type units joined by four bridging aza nitrogens, and each isoindole carries a linearly fused extra benzene ring, which makes four naphtho units. The two NH pyrrole nitrogens are the top-left and bottom-right units. The other two ring nitrogens, top-right and bottom-left, are unprotonated imine-type N atoms. No stereochemistry is drawn.

I checked the ring closures by hand. Each naphtho unit is written so that its two fusion carbons attach to the alpha carbons of the pyrrole ring. The Kekulé bond placement follows the standard H2Pc pattern and may differ in detail from the drawn double bonds, but the connectivity and hydrogen placement match.

name: rb_0011
text:
I read the molecule as a glutamic-acid-type core (free α-amine) with two different amide arms, each ending in the same indazole–imidazole unit.

**Central core:** H2N–CH(C(=O)–)–CH2–CH2–C(=O)–. This carbon is drawn with plain bonds, so it gets no stereo.

**Upper arm (from the γ-carbonyl):**
- The γ-carbonyl is bonded to NH–CH2CH2CH2–C(=O), a 4-aminobutanoyl (GABA) unit. I counted three CH2 groups.
- That carbonyl is bonded to NH–CH(COOH)–CH2–NH–C(=O)–, a 2,3-diaminopropionic acid unit.
- The carbonyl then attaches to C5 of an indazole.

**Lower arm (from the α-carbonyl):**
- The α-carbonyl is bonded to NH–(CH2)5–C(=O), a 6-aminohexanoyl unit. I counted five CH2 groups.
- That carbonyl is bonded to the same diaminopropionic acid unit (NH–CH(COOH)–CH2–NH–C(=O)–) and then to C5 of an indazole.

**Indazole and tail (both arms):** N1 of the indazole carries –CH2CH2CH2–NH–, which is bonded to C2 of a 1H-imidazole.

**Stereochemistry:**
- Upper diaminopropionic carbon: the CH2 is on a hashed bond, so the H points toward the viewer. The priority order N > COOH > CH2 runs clockwise, which reverses to counterclockwise, so the centre is S.
- Lower diaminopropionic carbon: the CH2 is on a wedge, so the H points away. The same priority order runs counterclockwise, so the centre is S.
- Both centres are therefore written as `N[C@H](C(=O)O)CN...`.

SMILES: NC(CCC(=O)NCCCC(=O)N[C@H](C(=O)O)CNC(=O)c1ccc2c(c1)cnn2CCCNc1ncc[nH]1)C(=O)NCCCCCC(=O)N[C@H](C(=O)O)CNC(=O)c1ccc2c(c1)cnn2CCCNc1ncc[nH]1

name: rb_0015
text:
The drawing shows a 2,2'-biphenyl core. Each of its phenyl rings is attached at the ortho position to a 3-substituted phenyl ring, and that ring carries a 1,10-phenanthrolin-2-yl group.

**Phenanthroline unit (left).** The pyridine ring containing N (at the bottom of the unit) is attached at C2 to the phenyl. The other nitrogen is in the left ring, and the two nitrogens sit in the 1,10 relationship. The SMILES for 1,10-phenanthrolin-2-yl is c1ccc2ccc3ccc(-Ar)nc3c2n1.

Checking the ring fusion:
- Ring A is n1cccc2 (N10, C9, C8, C7, C6a, C10a).
- The central ring carries C5=C6.
- Ring C is c3ccc(Ar)nc3, with C4a, C4, C3, C2 and N1.

**Linking.** The left phenyl is attached to phenanthroline C2 and, in the meta position, to biphenyl ring 1. Biphenyl ring 1 is bonded ortho to biphenyl ring 2, and ring 2 is bonded to the second meta-phenylene, which carries the second phenanthrolinyl group.

**SMILES assembly:**
- Phenanthrolinyl: c1cnc2c(c1)ccc1ccc(nc12)-
- Meta-phenylene: c1cccc(c1)-
- Biphenyl: c1ccccc1-c1ccccc1 (ortho-linked on both rings)

Full molecule: c1cnc2c(c1)ccc1ccc(nc12)-c1cccc(c1)-c1ccccc1-c1ccccc1-c1cccc(c1)-c1ccc2ccc3cccnc3c2n1

Checking the first phenanthroline: c1cnc2c(c1)ccc1ccc(nc12)-. Atoms: c1 (C), c (C), n (N), c2 (C10b-like), c(c1) closes the ring with the carbons, then ccc1ccc(nc12). In this fragment, n is bonded to c2, and c2 is bonded to the last c12, which is the carbon between the two nitrogens, so it is correct. The ring-closure digits are consistent: c12 closes ring 1 (the c1 after ccc) and ring 2.

The second phenanthrolinyl, c1ccc2ccc3cccnc3c2n1, is attached via its first atom c1, which is adjacent to n1 at the end. That makes it C2, bonded to N1, and the ring closures are consistent.

SMILES: c1cnc2c(c1)ccc1ccc(nc12)-c1cccc(c1)-c1ccccc1-c1ccccc1-c1cccc(c1)-c1ccc2ccc3cccnc3c2n1

name: rb_0013
text:

- **Indazole:** the propyl chain is on N1. The C5 carbonyl forms an amide with the NH of a 2,3-diaminopropionic acid unit.

**Assumptions**
- The "N" in the ethylene linker has no H drawn and only two visible bonds, so I wrote it as NH.
- Stereo is specified only at the two wedged centres.

name: rb_0016
text:
This is my reading of the drawing, with stereochemistry taken from the wedges and hashes where I could check them and otherwise assumed.

**Fragments read from the image**
- **Quinoline:** a 7-methoxy-2-phenylquinolin-4-yl group, attached through an ether oxygen to C4 of the pyrrolidine.
- **Pyrrolidine:** a proline-type ring with the aryloxy group at C4 and a carboxamide at C2. The ring nitrogen is acylated.
- **Acyl group on the ring nitrogen:** C(=O)–CH(O–C(=O)NH–C6H4–NMe2)–C(CH3)3. The carbamate is on the oxygen at the alpha carbon, and the aryl group is 4-(dimethylamino)phenyl.
- **Cyclopropane:** a 1-amino-2-vinylcyclopropane-1-carbonyl unit. Its carbonyl is bonded to NH–SO2–cyclopropyl (an acyl sulfonamide).

**Stereochemistry**

text:
The image shows a benzene ring carrying a vinyl group (CH=CH2, with the H drawn on the vinyl carbon) and two fluoroalkoxy substituents.

Numbering the vinyl carbon as C1, the two ether carbons are the ring vertex at the right (C4) and the vertex below it (C3). This gives a 3,4-disubstituted styrene.

Ring vertices:
- Top left, attached to the vinyl group: C1.
- Top: C2, which is H.
- Upper right: C3, which carries the O–CH2(CF2)6H chain at the "O" on the right.
- Lower right: C4, which carries the lower O–CH2(CF2)8H chain.
- Bottom: C5, which is H.
- Left: C6, which is H.

The drawing is a bit ambiguous about where the vinyl group sits. The vinyl attaches at the left vertex (about x=105, y=120). The ring vertices are approximately (135,70), (205,70), (235,125), (205,185), (135,185), (105,125). The vinyl is attached at (105,125). The upper O is attached at (235,125), which is para to the vinyl. The lower O is attached at (205,185), which is meta to the vinyl and adjacent to the para carbon.

So the ring is 1-vinyl, 4-O-CH2(CF2)6H, 3-O-CH2(CF2)8H.

Chain 2: OCH2 + 7 × CF2 + CF2H, which is OCC(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)F.

I read the structure region by region and assembled the SMILES below.

**Left end.** A tetrahydropyrimidine ring (six-membered: NH, CH2, CH2, CH2, N, and the C=N carbon). Its C2 carries an NH that connects to a propyl chain of three CH2 groups, which ends on N1 of the indazole.

**Indazole.** N1 bears the propyl chain and N2 is the =N. C3 is the CH, and the benzo ring carries a C(=O)NH group at C5.

**Amino acid core.** The amide NH is attached to CH2, then to a CH that carries the wedged CO2Me and an NH–SO2 group. This is a 2,3-diaminopropionic acid methyl ester.

**Aryl sulfonyl group.** The sulfonyl is on a benzene ring with methyls at both ortho positions. At the para position there is an O–CH2CH2CH2–C(=O)NH group.

**Right-hand chain.** The amide NH continues to CH2CH2, then NH–C(=O)–CH(NH2)–CH2CH2–C(=O)OtBu. The CH(NH2) is drawn with a wavy bond, so it has no defined stereo.

**Stereochemistry of the wedged carbon.** The wedged carbon has the CH2NH group to the left, the ester C to the upper right (wedge), and the NH below. I wrote the SMILES as NC[C@H](NS...)C(=O)OC and checked the chirality against the wedge. Viewed from the central carbon, the neighbors are CH2 (left, upper), NH (down) and C(ester) (right, wedge, toward the viewer), with H pointing away.

In the SMILES `NC[C@H](N)C(=O)OC`, the neighbor order is CH2, H, N, C(ester). With @, looking from CH2, the sequence H, N, C(ester) runs counterclockwise. Equivalently, the order CH2, N, C(ester) viewed with H away is determined by swapping H, which gives clockwise (@@ becomes @ on swapping). Since H is in the back, the drawing needs CH2 → N → C(ester) read in 2D: left-up, down, right. Going from upper left to down to right is counterclockwise on the page. That is the same as a counterclockwise reading viewed with H at the back (the wedge puts the ester toward the viewer, so H is behind).

For `[C@H]` with the order CH2, H, N, C: moving H to the front gives `[C@@H]`-style reordering (H, CH2, N, C is one swap, so @@). Looking from H, CH2 → N → C is then clockwise. Looking from the opposite side (H away), it is counterclockwise, which matches the drawing. So `[C@H]` is correct.

text:
Reading the structure region by region:

**Indazole core.** N1 carries a methyl group. N2 is the adjacent ring nitrogen, and C3 is attached to a CH2. The benzo ring carbon C6 carries the C(=O)NH group.

**C3 substituent.** C3 bears CH2–NH–C2 of an imidazole. The imidazole N1 carries a trityl group (C(Ph)3), and the ring is N1–C2(NH)=N3–C4=C5.

**Amino acid chain.** The amide NH is attached to CH2, then to the stereocentre CH(NH–SO2–Ar)C(=O)OCH3. The stereocentre is drawn with a wedge to the ester carbon.

**Aryl sulfonamide.** The sulfonamide is NH–SO2–C6H4–C6H4–SO2NH–CH2CH2NH2, a biphenyl with para substitution on both rings.

**Indazole SMILES.** Cn1nc(CNc2nccn2C(c2ccccc2)(c2ccccc2)c2ccccc2)c2ccc(C(=O)N...)cc12. In the drawing, N1 is bonded to C7a, which is bonded to C7 and then C6 (bearing the carbonyl). C3a is bonded to C4, then C5, then C6. So C6 is adjacent to C7, which is adjacent to C7a, which is bonded to N1. In the SMILES, c2ccc(C(=O)…)cc12 runs C3a, C4, C5, C6(C=O), C7, C7a, and this matches.

**Stereochemistry.** The stereocentre is written N[C@@H](CNC(=O)...)C(=O)OC, and I assign the chirality from the drawing. The centre has the CH2 to the upper left, the ester carbon to the right (wedge, toward the viewer), the NH below, and an implicit H.

Looking from the front with the H pointing away, the three substituents are the wedge substituent C(=O) (toward the viewer), CH2 (upper left) and N (down). Because the H is implicit, it points opposite to the wedge, i.e. away from the viewer. The priorities are N > C(=O)O (O,O,O) > CH2N (N,H,H) > H. In the 2D layout, N is at the bottom (about 270°), the ester carbon is at the right (about 0°, slightly up), and CH2 is at the upper left (about 150°). Going N (270°) → ester (0° or 360°) → CH2 (150°, or 510°) is increasing angle, so counterclockwise. With H pointing away, this gives S.

For the SMILES `N(...)[C@@H](CNC(=O)Ar)C(=O)OC`, the neighbours in order are N (preceding atom), H, CH2, C(=O). Viewed from N, the sequence H → CH2 → C(=O) is clockwise for @@. To check this against S, I permute the order to put H first: the order (N, H, CH2, CO) becomes (H, N, CH2, CO) after one swap, which flips the symbol to @. Viewed from H, N → CH2 → CO is then counterclockwise. Viewed from the side opposite H, it is clockwise, so N → CH2 → CO is clockwise. The priority order N → CO → CH2 is the reverse of this, so it is counterclockwise, which is S. So @@ gives S, which matches the drawing.

Starting from the form N, H, CH2, CO with @@, I permute to (CO, H, N, CH2). The mapping from (N, H, CH2, CO) to (CO, H, N, CH2) is a cyclic rotation of three elements (N → CH2 → CO), which is an even permutation, so the symbol stays @@.

I read the drawing as a cyclic depsipeptide. The ring is closed by an ester between the side-chain OH of D-Thr and the carboxyl of the L-Val that follows the Z-Dhb residue. An N-terminal 5-methylhexanoyl group caps the D-Val at the start of the chain.

Residue sequence, N-terminus to ring closure:

5-MeHex–D-Val–L-Thr–L-Val–D-Val–D-Pro–L-Orn–D-Ile–D-Thr–D-allo-Ile–D-Val–L-Phe–Z-Dhb–L-Val–(ester to the D-Thr side-chain oxygen)

I took the stereochemistry from the residue labels in the drawing (L/D, allo-Ile, Z-Dhb), not from the individual wedges. I derived the @/@@ tags from standard L- and D-amino-acid patterns. They have not been checked against a parser or against the wedge geometry.

SMILES: CC(C)CCCC(=O)N[C@H](C(C)C)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@@H](C)O)C(=O)N[C@@H](C(C)C)C(=O)N[C@H](C(C)C)C(=O)N1CCC[C@@H]1C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCN)C(=O)N[C@H]([C@@H](C)CC)C(=O)N[C@H]([C@H](C)O2)C(=O)N[C@H]([C@H](C)CC)C(=O)N[C@H](C(C)C)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)N/C(=C\C)C(=O)N[C@@H](C(C)C)C2=O

name: rb_0098
text:
The image shows 9,9'-spirobifluorene with a benzo[h]quinolin-2-yl group on the 2-position of each fluorene unit.

- **Spiro core:** the central sp3 carbon is shared by two fluorene units. Each fluorene has its substituent on the ring carbon that is para to the biaryl bond.
- **Substituents:** each benzo[h]quinoline is attached through C2, the carbon next to the nitrogen. The nitrogen sits next to the ring-fusion carbon that bears the terminal benzo ring, which is the benzo[h] arrangement.
- **Stereochemistry:** all bonds are drawn plain, so no stereo is specified. The spiro carbon is not a stereocentre because the two fluorenes are identical.

I wrote the SMILES in three parts and checked the ring closures and atom counts against the drawing:
- Unsubstituted fluorene: `C12(c3ccccc3-c3ccccc31)`
- Substituted fluorene: `c1cc(Ar)ccc1-c1ccc(Ar)cc12`
- Benzo[h]quinolin-2-yl (Ar): `c3ccc4ccc5ccccc5c4n3`

SMILES: C12(c3ccccc3-c3ccccc31)c1cc(-c3ccc4ccc5ccccc5c4n3)ccc1-c1ccc(-c3ccc4ccc5ccccc5c4n3)cc12

name: rb_0100
text:
I read the molecule as a ritonavir-type structure with an extra methyl on the carbon that bears the amide NH, and assigned each drawn stereocentre as follows.

**Connectivity, left to right:**
- A 2-isopropylthiazol-4-yl group, joined through CH2 to N(CH3).
- That N(CH3) carries a urea C=O, which links to the NH of a valine unit.
- The valine C=O forms an amide with an NH on a quaternary carbon that bears CH3 and CH2Ph.
- That carbon is followed by CH2, then CH(OH), then CH(CH2Ph)–NH.
- The terminal NH is a carbamate, NH–C(=O)–O–CH2, attached to thiazol-5-yl.

**Stereocentres (from the wedges and hashes):**
- Valine α-carbon: H hashed, isopropyl wedged. This gives S (L-valine), written `N[C@@H](C(C)C)C(=O)`.
- Quaternary carbon: CH3 wedged, benzyl hashed. This gives S, written `N[C@@](C)(Cc2ccccc2)C`.
- CH(OH): OH wedged. This gives S, written `C[C@H](O)`.
- CH(NH) carbon: H wedged. This gives S, written `[C@H](Cc2ccccc2)N`.

I assigned each centre by CIP priority and then converted to the @/@@ tags in the order the neighbours appear in the SMILES. I did not run the string through a parser, so validity rests on the manual check.

SMILES: CC(C)c1nc(CN(C)C(=O)N[C@@H](C(C)C)C(=O)N[C@@](C)(Cc2ccccc2)C[C@H](O)[C@H](Cc2ccccc2)NC(=O)OCc2cncs2)cs1

name: rb_0104
text:
I read the structure as a BTK-degrader PROTAC, with three regions: a tricyclic pyrazolo-benzodiazepine, a piperidine–piperazine linker, and a fluoro-thalidomide group.

**Tricyclic core (left).** A pyrazole carries a carboxamide (C(N)=O) on one carbon and a 4-phenoxyphenyl group on the adjacent carbon. The pyrazole ring is C3(C(N)=O)=C(Ar)–N=N... more precisely, the ring atoms are C(CONH2), C(Ar), N, N and the fused carbon. The ring N bonds to a CH2CH2 unit that leads to the benzene ring. The fused carbon bonds to an NH, and the NH bonds to the benzene ring, closing the seven-membered ring.

Pyrazole SMILES: c1(C(N)=O)c(Ar)nn2c1Nc1cc(C(=O)N...)ccc1CC2

Checking the seven-membered ring: pyrazole C(fused) – NH – benzene C – benzene C (ortho) – CH2 – CH2 – N(pyrazole). That is 7 atoms: C, N, C, C, CH2, CH2, N, which is correct.

**Benzene ring.** The NH-bearing carbon sits next to a CH carbon, which is next to the carbon bearing the carbonyl. The carbonyl-bearing carbon is meta to the NH carbon. The ring then continues through two CH carbons to the carbon attached to the CH2.

**Linker.** The carbonyl is an amide to a piperidine nitrogen. The piperidine C4 carries a CH2 that connects to a piperazine nitrogen. The other piperazine nitrogen is attached to the aryl ring of the isoindoline-1,3-dione.

**Thalidomide part.** The isoindoline aromatic ring carries F and the piperazine. The imide nitrogen bears a 2,6-dioxopiperidin-3-yl group.

**Full SMILES:**
NC(=O)c1c(-c2ccc(Oc3ccccc3)cc2)nn2c1Nc1cc(C(=O)N3CCC(CN4CCN(CC4)c4cc5C(=O)N(C6CCC(=O)NC6=O)C(=O)c5cc4F)CC3)ccc1CC2

For the isoindoline ring, the atoms are c4 (piperazine-bearing), c (CH), c5 (bearing C=O), c5' (bearing the other C=O), c (CH), c4F. The drawing shows F on the upper-left carbon and the piperazine on the lower-left carbon. The SMILES order is c4(N-pip) c c5(C(=O)N...C(=O)c5) c c4F. This puts F adjacent to the CH, which is adjacent to the ring-fusion carbon, and that matches the drawing.

SMILES: NC(=O)c1c(-c2ccc(Oc3ccccc3)cc2)nn2c1Nc1cc(C(=O)N3CCC(CN4CCN(CC4)c4cc5C(=O)N(C6CCC(=O)NC6=O)C(=O)c5cc4F)CC3)ccc1CC2

name: rb_0101
text:
I read the molecule as a macrocyclic peptide-like structure and wrote it as a single ring-closed SMILES.

**Ring components, in order around the macrocycle:**
- A diaminobutyric acid residue: H2N-CH2CH2-CH(NH-)-C(=O)-. Its alpha carbon carries the ring-closing NH-CH2 link to the pyridine.
- A lysine residue (free 4-aminobutyl side chain), joined to the first residue by an amide.
- An N-methyl tryptophan residue whose indole bears a 2-methyl group, joined through an N-methyl amide.
- Its C(=O)-NH-CH2 link to a benzene ring.
- The benzene ring, numbered from the CH2NH carbon:
  - C1 carries the CH2NH.
  - C2 carries the S to the pyridine.
  - C3 carries Cl.
  - C4 and C5 are CH.
  - C6 carries the pyridone.
- A pyridine joined through S at its C2, with CH2-NH at its C3, closing the ring back to the diaminobutyric acid alpha-NH.
- A 2-pyridone attached at its 4-position, with N-CH2-COOH.

**Stereochemistry:** The drawing shows wedges at three alpha carbons: the diaminobutyric acid, the lysine and the N-methyl tryptophan. In each case the wedged bond goes to the side chain. Working out the geometry from the 2D layout (hydrogen pointing back), each centre comes out as S, which is the L-amino acid configuration. No other stereo is drawn.

I checked the chirality tags in the SMILES against that: the diaminobutyric acid centre needed `[C@H]1` because of the order in which the ring-closure digit appears, and the other two are `[C@@H]`.

SMILES: NCC[C@H]1C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCCN)C(=O)N(C)[C@@H](Cc2c(C)[nH]c3ccccc23)C(=O)NCc4c(c(Cl)ccc4-c5ccn(CC(=O)O)c(=O)c5)Sc6ncccc6CN1

name: rb_0102
text:
I read the molecule from left to right as a peptide-like chain.

**Chain, from the C-terminus:**
- C-terminal penicillamine: a free carboxylic acid, an α-carbon bearing C(CH3)2SH, and an NH. The hashed bond to the CMe2SH carbon gives the R centre, i.e. L-penicillamine.
- Asp 1: CH2COOH side chain on a wedge bond, S configuration (L).
- Lys: a 4-carbon chain ending in NH2 (the side chain is (CH2)4NH2), drawn on a hashed bond, S configuration (L).
- Asp 2: CH2COOH side chain on a wedge bond, S configuration (L).
- Succinyl linker: NH–C(=O)CH2CH2C(=O)–NH.

**Quinoline and C-terminal cap:**
- The succinyl NH is attached at C8 of a quinoline.
- C4 of the quinoline carries C(=O)NH–CH2–C(=O)–, which is acylated onto a pyrrolidine nitrogen.
- The pyrrolidine has CF2 at C4 and a hashed nitrile at C2, which works out to S.

**Stereo encoding:** I wrote the SMILES from the penicillamine end. For that atom ordering I derived the tags by permuting the standard L-amino-acid pattern, which gives @ for the penicillamine, both Asp and the Lys centres. I checked the pyrrolidine C2 separately by CIP priorities (N > CN > CH2 > H), and @ gives S there.

SMILES: OC(=O)[C@H](C(C)(C)S)NC(=O)[C@H](CC(=O)O)NC(=O)[C@H](CCCCN)NC(=O)[C@H](CC(=O)O)NC(=O)CCC(=O)Nc1cccc2c(C(=O)NCC(=O)N3CC(F)(F)C[C@H]3C#N)ccnc12

name: rb_0103
text:
I read the structure in five parts and wrote each as SMILES.

1. **Left end:** a benzothiophene carrying a CF2–P(=O)(OH)2 group at C5. Its C2 carries an amide C(=O)NH.
2. **Bicyclic core:** a pyrrolidine fused to an eight-membered ring that contains an N-methyl nitrogen, a ring C=O and the NH-bearing stereocentre.
3. **Middle:** a glutamine residue (CH2CH2C(=O)NH2 side chain) joined by amide bonds.
4. **Linker:** an NH–CH(Ph) carbon, then a three-carbon chain to a piperidine nitrogen. The piperidine 4-position carries the alkyne.
5. **Right end:** an aryl alkyne on an isoindolinone, which is attached to a 2,6-dioxopiperidin-3-yl ring. The alkyne sits on the aromatic carbon next to the CH2-bearing ring-fusion carbon.

For stereochemistry I assigned @/@@ from the wedge bonds. There are five stereocentres: the ring-fusion carbon, the pyrrolidine CH bearing the carboxamide, the glutamine α-carbon, the CH(Ph) carbon and the NH-bearing carbon in the eight-membered ring. I assumed the wedge at CH(Ph) marks that carbon as the stereocentre. The piperidinyl-glutarimide carbon is drawn with plain bonds, so it has no stereo label.

SMILES: CN1CC[C@H]2CC[C@@H](C(=O)N[C@@H](CCC(N)=O)C(=O)N[C@@H](c3ccccc3)CCCN3CCC(CC3)C#Cc3cccc4c3CN(C3CCC(=O)NC3=O)C4=O)N2C(=O)[C@@H](NC(=O)c2cc3cc(C(F)(F)P(=O)(O)O)ccc3s2)C1

name: rb_0106
text:
This is a VHL-recruiting PROTAC-type molecule. I read it in four parts and joined them with the linker.

- **Left end:** a 4-cyanopyridin-2-yl group is attached through NH to a central pyridine. That pyridine carries a 3,3-difluoropyrrolidin-1-yl group on one side of the ring nitrogen and a piperidin-4-yl group on the other side.
- **Linker:** the piperidine nitrogen is acylated as N–C(=O)CH2CH2C(=O)–NH, a succinyl linker.
- **Tert-leucine unit:** the NH leads to a tert-butyl-bearing stereocentre, then C(=O) into the hydroxyproline nitrogen.
- **Right end:** a 4-hydroxyproline (hydroxyl drawn on a hashed bond) is joined by an amide to the (1-aryl)ethylamine. The aryl is a 4-(4-methylthiazol-5-yl)phenyl group.

For stereochemistry, I took the three drawn centres to be the standard VHL ligand configuration and checked the chirality tags against the known reference SMILES for that ligand. Each centre was compared after reordering its neighbours, and the tags in the answer match: tert-leucine S, hydroxyproline (2S,4R) and the benzylic methyl-bearing carbon S.

SMILES: N#Cc1ccnc(Nc2cc(C3CCN(CC3)C(=O)CCC(=O)N[C@@H](C(C)(C)C)C(=O)N3C[C@H](O)C[C@H]3C(=O)N[C@@H](C)c3ccc(cc3)-c3scnc3C)cc(n2)N2CCC(F)(F)C2)c1

name: rb_0105
text:
I read the drawing in four parts and wrote the SMILES by joining them.

- **Left end:** a 4-cyanopyridin-2-yl group joined through NH to a second pyridine. That pyridine carries a 3,3-difluoropyrrolidin-1-yl group at C6 and a piperidin-4-yl group at C4.
- **Linker:** the piperidine nitrogen is acylated by a 4-(aminomethyl)benzoyl group, and the benzylic nitrogen is a secondary amine.
- **Central amino acid:** that amine is attached to the alpha carbon of a tert-leucine unit, whose carbonyl forms the amide to the pyrrolidine nitrogen.
- **Right end:** a 4-hydroxypyrrolidine-2-carboxamide whose amide nitrogen carries a 1-[4-(4-methylthiazol-5-yl)phenyl]ethyl group.

I assigned stereochemistry from the wedges and hashes, using CIP priorities with the hydrogen pointing away from the viewer:

- **tert-Leucine alpha carbon:** S.
- **Pyrrolidine C2:** S, from the wedged carboxamide.
- **Pyrrolidine C4:** R, from the hashed OH, giving the trans-4-hydroxy-L-proline pattern.
- **Benzylic CH(CH3) carbon:** S, from the wedged methyl.

I then wrote each centre in SMILES and checked its @/@@ symbol against these assignments. That check showed the initial tert-leucine, C4 and benzylic centres needed their symbols reversed, and the final string below uses the corrected ones.

name: rb_0110
text:
I read the image region by region and assembled the SMILES below. I did not run it through a parser, so validity is checked by hand only.

**Left to right:**
- **Pyridine core:** a 2,4,6-trisubstituted pyridine. Position 2 carries an NH link to a 4-cyanopyridin-2-yl group. Position 4 carries the piperidine. Position 6 carries a 3,3-difluoropyrrolidin-1-yl group.
- **Linker:** the piperidine nitrogen is acylated by a 1,4-phenylene carbonyl. The other carbonyl of the phenylene is an amide to the nitrogen of the tert-leucine unit.
- **tert-Leucine unit:** it carries the tert-butyl group and is drawn with a wedge. Its carbonyl acylates the proline nitrogen.
- **Hydroxyproline:** the 4-hydroxyl is drawn with a hashed bond. Its 2-carboxamide is bound to the NH of the 1-arylethyl group.
- **Right end:** a 1-(4-(4-methylthiazol-5-yl)phenyl)ethyl group, with its methyl drawn on a wedge.

**Stereochemistry:** the drawing has four stereocentres, all with wedges or hashes. They match the usual (2S,4R)-hydroxyproline, (S)-tert-leucine and (S)-1-arylethylamine of VHL ligands such as VH298. I took the @/@@ tags from the standard VH298 SMILES rather than deriving them from the drawing.

name: rb_0108
text:
The SMILES below was read from the drawing region by region.

- **Core:** a BF2 complex of two benzo-fused (isoindole-type) pyrrole units bridged by a meso carbon. One nitrogen is neutral and bonded to boron. The other is N+ and is double-bonded to its benzo carbon, so that benzo ring is drawn quinoid. Boron carries the negative charge and two fluorines.
- **Meso substituent:** a phenyl ring attached at C1, with a methoxy group at C3 and the macrocycle nitrogen at C4.
- **Macrocycle:** a 1,10-diaza-crown ring. Going round from the aryl-bearing N: CH2CH2–O–CH2CH2–N(2-methoxyphenyl)–CH2CH2–O–CH2CH2–O–CH2CH2 back to the first N.
- **Stereochemistry:** none is shown in the drawing, so none is included.

I checked the ring-closure digits so that each is closed before it is reused, and the atom count matches the drawing.

name: rb_0111
text:
I read the drawing as a VHL-type ligand (tert-leucine, hydroxyproline and a 1-(4-(4-methylthiazol-5-yl)phenyl)ethylamine) attached through a thiophene and piperazine to an aminopyridazine bearing a 2-hydroxyphenyl group.

- **Left end:** a pyridazine with NH2 on one carbon next to a ring nitrogen, a piperazine nitrogen on the next carbon, and a 2-hydroxyphenyl on the carbon beyond the CH. The piperazine's other nitrogen is bonded to C5 of a thiophene, and C2 of the thiophene carries the carboxamide.
- **Middle:** the amide NH is attached to a tert-leucine unit, which is acylated onto the nitrogen of a 4-hydroxypyrrolidine-2-carboxamide.
- **Right end:** that carboxamide NH is bonded to a CH(CH3) carbon, which is attached to a para-substituted phenyl ring carrying a 4-methylthiazol-5-yl group.

I did not trace each wedge and hash individually. I assigned the stereochemistry as the standard VHL-ligand configuration (S at tert-leucine, 2S,4R at hydroxyproline, S at the phenylethylamine carbon) and checked that the drawing is consistent with it. I then converted that standard SMILES to my atom ordering by counting neighbour-order permutations at each stereocentre.

name: rb_0107
text:
I read the structure in sections and assembled the SMILES from them.

**Left to right:**

- The central pyridine carries a 3,3-difluoropyrrolidin-1-yl group at C6 and a piperidin-4-yl group at C4.

name: rb_0114
text:
I read the molecule as these fragments, joined in order:

- **Left end:** a cyclohexyl group on a phenyl ring, which carries a sulfonamide (SO2–NH) on the para position.
- **Middle aryl:** the sulfonamide NH is attached to a para-substituted benzene ring, which carries a CH2 group.
- **Stereocentre:** the CH2 leads to a carbon bearing NH2 (drawn with a wedge) and a C(=O) group. By CIP priorities (N > C(=O) > CH2 > H, with H pointing away), the wedge gives the S configuration, which in this SMILES is written `[C@@H]`.
- **Piperidine:** the C(=O) forms an amide with a piperidine nitrogen. The piperidine is substituted at C4 by a CH2CH2 chain.
- **Alkyne:** the chain ends in a C≡C triple bond.
- **Isoindolinone:** the alkyne attaches to the isoindolinone benzene ring at the carbon next to the one bearing the CH2 of the five-membered ring (position 4). The lactam carbonyl is on the other side of the fused ring.
- **Glutarimide:** the isoindolinone nitrogen carries a 2,6-dioxopiperidin-3-yl group. Its stereocentre is drawn with plain bonds, so I give it no stereo label.

name: rb_0113
text:
This SMILES was read region by region from the drawing. I did not run it through a parser, so the validity check was done by hand.

- **Left end:** a pyrazine-2-carboxamide with a piperidin-1-yl group and an anilino NH. The aniline ring carries a 4-piperidinyl group, and that piperidine nitrogen starts a –CH2CH2OCH2CH2OCH2C(=O)– linker.
- **Centre:** a tert-leucine amide joined to a 4-hydroxyproline amide, then a benzylamide. The benzene ring has the thiazole para to the CH2 and the ether oxygen ortho. The thiazole is 4-methylthiazol-5-yl. I took the stereocentres as the standard VHL-ligand configuration, matching the wedges and hashes drawn. I checked the neighbour order of each centre against the standard form of that ligand.
- **Right end:** the ether oxygen continues through –CH2CH2OCH2CH2N(CH3)CH2– to a cyclohexane. The cyclohexane is drawn trans-1,4 (one wedge, one hash) and is bonded to N2 of a 2H-indazole. The indazole carries the 6-(2-hydroxypropan-2-yl) group and, at C5, an amide to 6-(trifluoromethyl)picolinic acid.

name: rb_0112
text:
I read the molecule as a PROTAC-type structure with five parts:

- **VHL ligand:** a 4-hydroxyproline with the (2S,4R)-style stereochemistry of VH032. Its amide nitrogen carries a 4-(4-methylthiazol-5-yl)benzyl group, and its ring nitrogen is acylated by tert-leucine.
- **Urea link:** the tert-leucine NH forms a urea with a nitrogen that carries two four-carbon chains.
- **First chain:** the chain runs to a secondary amine (NH), then a CH2, then a trans-1,4-cyclohexane. The ring ends in an indazole N2 that has a 6-(2-hydroxypropan-2-yl) group and a 5-NHC(=O)-6-(trifluoromethyl)pyridin-2-yl amide.
- **Second chain:** the chain runs to a piperidine nitrogen, and the piperidine C4 is bonded to a para-phenylene.
- **Pyrazine end:** the phenylene NH is bonded to a pyrazine bearing a carboxamide and a piperidin-1-yl group.

Stereochemistry:

- **Proline and tert-leucine centres:** these follow the VH032 pattern.
- **Cyclohexane:** the wedge at the indazole-bearing carbon and the hash at the CH2-bearing carbon make it trans. I assigned the two `@` marks from the drawn geometry.

I checked the ring closures and atom counts, and the SMILES should be valid.

name: rb_0115
text:
I read the structure as a macrocyclic peptide-like molecule and built the SMILES from its parts.

**Fragments**
- **Ornithine residue:** NH2–(CH2)3–CH, with its α-NH linked through a CH2 to the 3-position of a pyridine. The drawing shows three chain CH2 groups, so this is ornithine.
- **Lysine residue:** NH2–(CH2)4–CH, whose α-NH is acylated by the ornithine C=O. There are four chain CH2 groups.
- **N-methyl tryptophan:** the lysine C=O joins the N-methyl nitrogen. The side chain is CH2 to indol-3-yl.

text:
I read the drawing as a C2-symmetric cyclic depsipeptide of the echinomycin type, with a thioacetal cross-bridge and two quinoxaline-2-carboxamide chromophores. No wedges or hashes are drawn, so the SMILES carries no stereochemistry.

**Bridge.** One N-methyl-cysteine-derived α-carbon (A, top centre) carries a β-carbon that bears both an SMe group and a ring sulfur. That sulfur links through a CH2 to the other α-carbon (Cα′, bottom centre), which has its own N-methyl.

**Ring around the bridge.** Going round from A:
- A's N-methyl nitrogen is acylated by Ala (with its NH), then a Ser (with a CH2O ester oxygen), which is the left-hand Ser carrying the quinoxaline-2-carboxamide (NH–CO–quinoxaline) on its α-carbon.
- That Ser's oxygen forms an ester with the carboxyl of an N-methyl-valine, whose N-methyl nitrogen is acylated by the C(=O) of Cα′.
- The right-hand half is the same sequence: Cα′'s N-methyl nitrogen is acylated by Ala, then the second quinoxaline-bearing Ser, then ester-linked N-methyl-valine. This valine's N-methyl nitrogen is acylated by the C(=O) of A, closing the ring.

**Check.** The SMILES has one closed macrocycle through both halves and the bridge, two quinoxaline rings, two isopropyl groups, four N-methyls, two Ala methyls and one SMe, matching the drawing atom for atom.

SMILES: CSC1SCC2N(C)C(=O)C(C)NC(=O)C(NC(=O)c3cnc4ccccc4n3)COC(=O)C(C(C)C)N(C)C(=O)C1N(C)C(=O)C(C)NC(=O)C(NC(=O)c1cnc3ccccc3n1)COC(=O)C(C(C)C)N(C)C2=O

name: rb_0146
text:
I read the molecule as a macrocyclic peptide with three amino acid residues closed through an aryl–thioether–pyrazine linker.

**Residues in the ring**
- **Ornithine:** its α-carbon carries a H2N-CH2CH2CH2 side chain, drawn on a wedge. Its α-NH is bonded to a CH2 on the pyrazine, and its C=O is bonded to the lysine NH.
- **Lysine:** its α-carbon carries a (CH2)4NH2 side chain, drawn on a wedge. Its C=O is bonded to the N-methyl nitrogen of the next residue.
- **N-methyl tryptophan:** its α-carbon carries a CH2-(indol-3-yl) side chain, drawn on a wedge. Its C=O is bonded to an NH, which is bonded to a CH2 on the benzene ring.

**Linker**
- **Pyrazine:** the ring is 2,3-disubstituted. One carbon carries the CH2 from the ornithine NH, and the adjacent carbon carries the sulfur.
- **Benzene:** going round the ring, the carbons carry CH2NH, then S, then Cl, then two CH, then a 4-carboxyphenyl group, which sits next to the CH2NH carbon.

**Stereochemistry**
- Working from the wedges, all three α-carbons come out as S, matching the natural L-amino acids.
- I converted each to the correct @/@@ in the SMILES by ordering the neighbours as written. This gives @@ for ornithine, @ for lysine and @ for tryptophan.

name: rb_0145
text:
I read the structure in four parts and wrote the SMILES from them.

**Left macrocycle ring (cyano-fluoro benzene).** The ring carries the C≡N and an F. Its two ortho substituents are a CH2CH2–O chain and a CH2–O group, which links to the pyridine oxygen.

**Central fluoro benzene.** One ring carbon bears the CH2 that connects to the ether O. Its neighbour carbon bears the pyridin-2-yl group. The ring also has an F and a CH2 that leads to the benzimidazole.

**Pyridine.** It is 2,6-disubstituted: C2 is bonded to the central benzene, and C6 carries the O that connects through CH2 to the cyano ring.

**Benzimidazole.**
- C2 bears the CH2 from the central benzene.
- N1 bears the CH2 attached to the oxetan-2-yl group.
- C4 bears OCH2CH2OCH3.
- C6 bears CO2H.

**Stereocentre.** The only wedge or hash in the drawing is the hashed bond from the N–CH2 to the oxetane C2. The CIP priorities are O, then CH2N, then ring CH2, then H. With the hashed CH2N pointing back and the implicit H toward the viewer, the centre is S. In the SMILES this corresponds to `[C@@H]`.

The macrocycle ring closures, the benzimidazole substitution pattern and the stereo tag were each checked against this reading.

name: rb_0148
text:
I read the molecule as a DOTA-type macrocycle linked through a 4-aminopiperidine to a peptide chain that ends in prolinamide. I checked each stereocentre against the wedges and hashes.

**Fragments, left to right**
- **Macrocycle:** a 12-membered ring with four nitrogens (cyclen). Three nitrogens carry CH2COOH arms, and the fourth carries CH2C(=O)NH– to the next fragment.
- **Linker:** a piperidine joined through its C4 amine to that acetamide, with its ring nitrogen bearing CH2C(=O)–.
- **Peptide chain:** D-Phe, then L-Gln, then α-methyl-L-Trp (a quaternary carbon bearing a methyl, drawn with a wedge to the CH2). Next come L-Ala, L-tert-leucine (a tert-butyl side chain), Gly and 5-fluoro-L-Trp.
- **C-terminus:** a reduced leucine, –NH–CH(CH2CH(CH3)2)–CH2–, in which the carbonyl is replaced by CH2 and the carbon is R as drawn. This CH2 is bonded to the nitrogen of an L-prolinamide, N1CCC[C@H]1C(=O)N.

**Stereochemistry as read from the drawing**
- D-Phe is R, and the L-amino acids (Gln, α-Me-Trp, Ala, tert-leucine, 5F-Trp, Pro) are all S.
- The reduced-leucine carbon comes out R from the wedge on its isobutyl bond.

name: rb_0149
text:
I read this as a rifamycin-type ansa macrolide fused to a phenoxazine ring (a rifamycin S–aminophenol condensation product).

**Core.** The aromatic part is a naphthoquinone-like ring system. A furanone ring carries a quaternary carbon with a methyl and the ether oxygen (wedge bond). A methyl and a hydroxyl sit on the benzene ring. A phenoxazine unit carries a hydroxyl on its outer benzene ring and is fused to the quinone ring. The quinone ring bears the amide NH.

**Ansa chain.** Starting from the amide nitrogen, the chain runs:
- C(=O)–C(CH3)=CH–CH=CH
- then CH(CH3), CH(OH), CH(CH3), CH(OH), CH(CH3), CH(OAc), CH(CH3), CH(OMe)
- then CH=CH–O, which returns to the quaternary ketal carbon.

**Double bonds.** The CH=CH next to the methyl-bearing alkene is trans. The methyl-bearing alkene is drawn cis between the carbonyl carbon and the following chain carbon, so I wrote it as Z.

**Stereocentres.** I assigned the `@`/`@@` tags by analogy with natural rifamycin rather than by tracing each wedge in the drawing, so those tags are less certain than the connectivity.

text:
I read the structure region by region and wrote it as the SMILES below. I did not run it through a parser. The stereocentres at the cyano-pyrrolidine carbon and the Asp, Lys and Cys α-carbons are assigned from the drawn wedges and the expected natural configurations, not independently verified.

**Reading of the structure, left to right:**
1. A (S)-2-cyano-4,4-difluoropyrrolidine, with its nitrogen acylated by a glycyl group.
2. That glycine nitrogen forms an amide to the carbonyl at C4 of a quinoline.
3. The quinoline C8 carries an NH-succinyl linker (NH–CO–CH2CH2–CO).
4. The succinyl group leads into a peptide chain: Asp, then Lys (free side-chain NH2), then Asp, then Cys. Each residue's side chain is drawn as in the image, and the chain ends in the Cys free carboxylic acid.
5. The Cys sulfur is bonded to C3 of a succinimide ring (a thiol–maleimide adduct).
6. The succinimide nitrogen carries an N-ethyl chain, which ends in an amide NH–CO–CH2CH2–CH(COOH).
7. That CH(COOH) is bonded to one nitrogen of a 1,4,7-triazacyclononane ring. The other two ring nitrogens each carry a CH2COOH group (a NODAGA-type chelator).

text:

text:

4. **Second lysine:** it has a free CO2H, and its ε-NH carries a 4-iodophenylacetyl group. The wedge geometry again gives S, so this is also L-lysine.

I checked the quinoline connectivity: C7 sits between C6 and C8, and C4 sits next to C4a. The cyclen ring also closes correctly. I did not run the SMILES through a parser.

- **Left side:** a 4-cyanopyridin-2-yl group is attached through NH to a second pyridine. That pyridine carries a 3,3-difluoropyrrolidin-1-yl group at C6 and a piperidin-4-yl group at C4.
- **Linker:** the piperidine nitrogen is acylated by a trans-1,2-disubstituted cyclobutane. The first carbon is hashed to its C=O (the piperidine amide). The second carbon is wedged to its carboxamide, whose NH leads to the tert-leucine.
- **tert-Leucine:** the alpha carbon carries a wedged NH, a tert-butyl group and a C=O. I assigned it S.
- **Hydroxyproline:** it is acylated on nitrogen by the tert-leucine and bears the hydroxyl at C4. I assigned (2S,4R) from the wedges.
- **Right side:** the proline C=O forms an amide with an (S)-1-[4-(4-methylthiazol-5-yl)phenyl]ethylamine. The wedged methyl gives S.

I derived the SMILES chirality tags by comparing each drawn centre with the atom order written in the SMILES.

name: rb_0188
text:
I read the drawing left to right and wrote the SMILES in that order. The linker order is:

1. Maleimide, joined through N to a five-CH2 chain and then a C=O (a 6-maleimidocaproyl amide).
2. A glutamic acid residue whose side-chain amide is N-methyl on a five-hydroxyl open-chain polyol (an N-methylglucamine-type unit).
3. Three alanine residues in a row.
4. An NH–CH2–O–CH2–C(=O)–NH spacer.
5. A camptothecin-type core. It carries SMe and F on the benzo ring, the CH2NH linker at the C7 position, and the lactone C(Et)(OH).

I assigned stereochemistry only at the drawn wedge/hash centres:

- **Polyol:** the four hydroxyl-bearing carbons come out as (S) at the first carbon (counting from the N-methyl end), with the other three consistent with the N-methylglucamine pattern.
- **Glutamic acid:** L configuration.
- **Alanines:** all three are L.
- **Lactone quaternary carbon:** I assumed the natural (S)-camptothecin configuration. The Et and OH bond depiction was hard to read.

I did not run the SMILES through a parser. I checked the ring closures by hand and worked out the chirality tags from the drawn 2D geometry.

I read the structure region by region and wrote it as the SMILES below. I did not run it through a parser, so validity is checked only by hand.

- **Left end:** a glutarimide (2,6-dioxopiperidin-3-yl) on the nitrogen of an isoindoline-1,3-dione.
- **Isoindoline ring:** one aromatic carbon carries an NH–CH2CH2 chain. The next carbon carries an azetidine nitrogen.
- **Spiro linker:** the ethyl chain ends on a 2-azaspiro[3.3]heptane, attached at the cyclobutane CH. The azetidine nitrogen of the spiro unit bears a CH2 that leads to a cyclohexane.
- **Cyclohexane:** it is 1,4-disubstituted with one wedged and one hashed bond, which makes it trans. I encoded this as `[C@H]…[C@H]`. The absolute configuration is a best guess from the wedge/hash drawing.
- **Right end of the cyclohexane:** the cyclohexane carries a benzothiazole at C2. The benzothiazole has a 2-hydroxypropan-2-yl group and an NH–C(=O) link to a 6-(trifluoromethyl)pyridine-2-yl group.
- **Lower branch:** the azetidine nitrogen on the isoindoline is linked through azetidine C3 to a piperidine nitrogen. Piperidine C4 carries a para-phenylene, which is joined through NH to a pyrazine. The pyrazine carries a carboxamide and a piperidin-1-yl group.

name: rb_0194
text:
I read the molecule as a capped tetrapeptide linked through a self-immolative benzyl ether to a spiro-adamantyl dioxetane (a Schaap-type caged chemiluminescent probe).

**Fragments, left to right**
- The N-terminus is an acetyl group on the amine of a 2-indanylglycine residue.
- Next is 4-chlorophenylalanine.
- Next is lysine, with a free terminal NH2 on its four-carbon side chain.
- Next is leucine, whose C-terminus forms an anilide with a para-substituted aniline.
- The aniline's para CH2 is bonded to an aryl ether oxygen.
- On that aryl ring, the carbon bearing the ether oxygen is flanked by a chlorine-bearing carbon and by the carbon carrying the (E)-CH=CH–CO2Me group.
- Next to the chlorine-bearing carbon is the dioxetane carbon, which also carries OMe. The dioxetane is spiro-fused to adamantane at its 2-position.

**Stereochemistry**
- I assigned the four peptide α-carbons from the wedges and hashes.
- Indanylglycine and lysine have the side chain on a wedge, with N on the left and C=O on the right. Both are S.
- 4-Chlorophenylalanine and leucine have the side chain on a hash, with N on the upper left or left and C=O on the right. Both are S, the natural L configuration.
- The acrylate double bond is drawn trans, so I wrote it as E.
- The dioxetane carbon bearing OMe and the aryl ring is drawn with plain bonds, so it has no stereo label.

I checked the adamantane SMILES by counting atoms: 10 carbons, 4 bridgehead CH and 6 CH2 including the spiro carbon.

name: rb_0196
text:
Reading the structure region by region:

- **Macrocycle:** a cyclen (1,4,7,10-tetraazacyclododecane) ring. Three nitrogens carry CH2C(=O)NH2 arms. The fourth carries CH2C(=O)NH–CH2–, which links to the cyclohexane.
- **Cyclohexane:** 1,4-disubstituted, bearing the CH2NH group at one position and C(=O)NH at the other. No stereochemistry is drawn.
- **Amino acid:** the C(=O)NH– from the cyclohexane acylates the α-amine of a 2-naphthylalanine. Its carbonyl forms an amide with NH–(CH2)4–, which is the lysine side-chain amine.
- **Urea:** the lysine α-carbon carries NH–C(=O)–NH–, the other side of which is the glutamate α-carbon. Lysine has its COOH, and glutamate has COOH on the α-carbon plus a CH2CH2COOH side chain.

Chain check from the lysine amine: NH–CH2 (the bond leaves NH), then CH2, CH2, CH2, then CH(COOH). In the image, NH–CH2 is followed by three more vertices before the CH(COOH). That gives four CH2 groups, as in lysine.

SMILES assembly:

NC(=O)CN1CCN(CC(=O)NCC2CCC(CC2)C(=O)NC(Cc2ccc3ccccc3c2)C(=O)NCCCCC(NC(=O)NC(CCC(=O)O)C(=O)O)C(=O)O)CCN(CC(N)=O)CCN(CC(N)=O)CC1

Ring check: N1, CC, N(arm), CC, N, CC, N, CC back to N1. In the SMILES, N1CCN(...)CCN(...)CCN(...)CC1 contains four nitrogens, each separated by two carbons. The first nitrogen has the NC(=O)C arm, the second the linker arm, and the third and fourth have amide arms, so three amide arms and one linker arm in total, as drawn.

SMILES: NC(=O)CN1CCN(CC(=O)NCC2CCC(CC2)C(=O)NC(Cc2ccc3ccccc3c2)C(=O)NCCCCC(NC(=O)NC(CCC(=O)O)C(=O)O)C(=O)O)CCN(CC(N)=O)CCN(CC(N)=O)CC1

name: rb_0186
text:
The SMILES below was read from the drawing as a rifamycin-type macrocycle fused to a phenoxazine. I have not run it through a validator, so the checks listed here were done by hand.

**Core and substituents**
- The core is a naphthofuranone ring system fused to a phenoxazine. The furanone ring carries a C=O and a quaternary carbon bearing a methyl group.
- The aromatic ring carries one methyl and one OH.
- The six-membered quinone ring carries an exocyclic C=O and the NH amide link.
- The phenoxazine has an N=C bond, a ring O, and a benzene ring bearing O–CH2CH2–O–CH2CH2–N(CH3)2 para to the ring N.

**Ansa chain** (counted from the amide)

- Then CH(CH3), CH(OH), CH(CH3), CH(OH), CH(CH3), CH(OAc), CH(CH3) and CH(OMe).
- It ends in a trans CH=CH–O that links to the quaternary acetal carbon.

**Stereochemistry:** each centre was set from the drawn wedges and hashes. The vinyl-ether C=C is trans.

name: rb_0193
text:
This SMILES is my best reading of the drawing, with some uncertain points that I list below. The structure is a bicyclic peptide made of these parts:

- **N-terminal cap:** a hexanoyl group on the N-terminal Cys. I counted six carbons including the C=O, but the end of the chain at the top right is hard to read.
- **Peptide sequence:** hexanoyl-Cys-Pro-Pro-Thr-Gln-Phe-Cys-Asp-NH2, with the C-terminal Asp as a primary amide.
- **Core:** the two Cys thiols are each linked through S-CH2 to a 1,3,5-trisubstituted benzene. This closes the macrocycle.
- **Third benzene arm:** it carries a CH2 on one nitrogen of a piperazine. The other piperazine nitrogen is acylated by C(=O)CH2 to a DOTA-type tetraaza macrocycle.
- **Lutetium:** Lu is bonded to all four ring nitrogens and to the three remaining acetate oxygens. The fourth arm is the amide.

Points I could not settle:

- **Stereochemistry:** I wrote every residue as L, which matches the wedge on the first Cys. The Thr alpha centre and some other residues are drawn with hashes that I could not read reliably.
- **Lu–N bonds:** I wrote them as plain single bonds, which gives the ring nitrogens four bonds on neutral atoms. I chose this over dropping the bonds so the Lu coordination stays in the string. A strict valence checker may flag it.

name: rb_0199
text:
I read the structure as a VHL-ligand-based degrader-type molecule, working from left to right.

**Left side**
- A 4-cyanopyridin-2-yl group is attached through an NH to C2 of a central pyridine.
- C6 of that central pyridine carries a 3,3-difluoropyrrolidin-1-yl group.
- C4 of the central pyridine is bonded to C4 of a piperidine.

**Middle**
- The piperidine nitrogen is acylated by a para-substituted benzoyl group.
- The other para position of that benzene bears CH2–NH, which is bonded to the tert-leucine α-carbon.

**Right side (VHL ligand)**
- The tert-leucine unit has a tert-butyl group and an amide to the pyrrolidine nitrogen.
- The pyrrolidine is a 4-hydroxyproline, and its C2 carries a carboxamide.
- That amide nitrogen is bonded to a CH(CH3) group attached to a phenyl ring, which carries a 4-methylthiazol-5-yl group.

**Stereochemistry**
I assigned each centre from the wedges and hashes in the drawing:
- The tert-leucine α-carbon (wedge to N) is S.
- Proline C2 (wedge to the carboxamide) is S.
- Proline C4 (hashed OH) is R.
- The CH(CH3) carbon (wedged methyl) is S.

These match the usual (2S,4R)-hydroxyproline and (S)-1-arylethylamide pattern of VHL ligands. I wrote the SMILES with matching chirality tags and checked ring closures and parentheses.

name: rb_0200
text:
I read the structure in four pieces and joined them.

- **Left end:** a 4-phenoxyphenyl group sits on a dihydro pyrazolo[1,5-a][1,3]benzodiazepine, with a primary carboxamide on the pyrazole carbon next to it. The ring NH is drawn explicitly.
- **Benzodiazepine benzo ring:** the amide carbonyl is on the carbon para to the NH-bearing carbon and meta to the CH2-bearing carbon. I checked this against the ring vertices in the drawing.
- **Linker:** a C(=O)NH group leads to a 1,4-disubstituted cyclohexane. One substituent is drawn with a wedge and the other with a hash, so the ring is trans. The other cyclohexane substituent is a CH2 attached to a piperazine nitrogen.
- **Right end:** the piperazine's other nitrogen is bonded to a fluoro-substituted isoindoline-1,3-dione (the fluorine is on the carbon adjacent to the piperazine-bearing carbon). The isoindoline nitrogen carries a 2,6-dioxopiperidin-3-yl group, drawn with no stereochemistry.

For the trans ring I wrote `N[C@H]1CC[C@H](CN...)CC1`. I derived this ordering by working through the chirality of each ring carbon, using the pattern `C[C@H]1CC[C@H](C)CC1` for trans-1,4 disubstitution.

name: rb_0202
text:
I read the structure region by region, from left to right.

**Left fragment.** A 6-methylpyridin-2-yl group is bonded through NH to a C(=O) attached to a benzene ring. Numbering the benzene from the amide-bearing carbon (C1): C2 carries a methyl, C3 carries F, and C4 is bonded to the pyrazole carbon. This gives Cc1cccc(n1)NC(=O)c1ccc(c(F)c1C)-.

**Central tricycle.** The pyrazole contains C2 (bearing the aryl group), C3 (bearing C(N)=O), C3a, N1 and N2. C3a is bonded to the NH, which is bonded to the benzo ring. The benzo ring is connected through CH2CH2 to N1 of the pyrazole, forming a 7-membered ring: C3a, NH, benzo C, benzo C, CH2, CH2, N1.

SMILES for this part: NC(=O)c1c(-aryl)nn2CCc3cc(ccc3Nc12)-N...

Checking the ring closures: c1(C(N)=O) is C3, c(-Ar) is C2, n is N2, and n2 is N1 with the CH2CH2. Then c3 is the benzo carbon attached to the CH2, followed by cc(...)ccc3, where the piperazine-bearing carbon is the second atom after c3. The ring continues cc c3 N c12. From the drawing, the piperazine-bearing carbon is para to the NH-bearing carbon, which fits this connectivity: the benzo carbon attached to CH2, then CH, then C(N-pip), then CH, CH, and C(NH).

**Right fragment.** The piperazine N' is bonded to azetidine C3. That azetidine's N is bonded to the C3 of a second azetidine, whose N is bonded to the isoindoline-1,3-dione ring at position 5. The imide N carries a 2,6-dioxopiperidin-3-yl group.

**Assembled SMILES:**
Cc1cccc(n1)NC(=O)c1ccc(c(F)c1C)-c1nn2CCc3cc(ccc3Nc2c1C(N)=O)N1CCN(CC1)C1CN(C1)C1CN(C1)c1ccc2C(=O)N(C3CCC(=O)NC3=O)C(=O)c2c1

name: rb_0197
rb_0205
text:
The drawing is a BTK-degrader PROTAC. It has a pyrazolo-benzodiazepine core linked through a piperazine amide and a piperidine to a thalidomide-type ligand.

**Core.** The pyrazole ring contains C3 (bearing the carboxamide), C2 (bearing the 4-phenoxyphenyl group), N, and N1, plus the fused carbon attached to NH.
- The pyrazole carbon bearing C(=O)N is bonded to the pyrazole carbon bearing the NH, and the other pyrazole carbon bears the aryl group.
- The ring N1 bonds to CH2CH2, which connects to the benzo ring.
- The seven-membered ring runs: pyrazole C (attached to NH), NH, aryl C, aryl C, CH2, CH2, N1 (pyrazole).

Pyrazole SMILES: c1(C(N)=O)c(-c2ccc(Oc3ccccc3)cc2)nn3c1Nc4ccc(cc4CC3)C(=O)...

Here the pyrazole atoms are c1 (carboxamide carbon), c(Ar), n, n3, and c1 (the carbon bonded to NH).

**Benzo ring.** The NH-bearing aromatic carbon is c4. The ring then continues ccc(C=O)cc4 with the CH2 attached at the final ring carbon. In the drawing, the carbonyl-bearing carbon is para to the NH-bearing carbon's neighbor, which is consistent with this layout.

**Linker.** The carbonyl is attached to a piperazine N. The other piperazine N carries a CH2 that leads to piperidine C4. The piperidine N is bonded to the isoindoline-1,3-dione at position 5. The isoindoline N bears the 2,6-dioxopiperidin-3-yl group.

**Assembly.**
NC(=O)c1c(-c2ccc(Oc3ccccc3)cc2)nn2CCc3cc(ccc3Nc12)C(=O)N1CCN(CC1)CC1CCN(CC1)c1ccc2C(=O)N(C3CCC(=O)NC3=O)C(=O)c2c1

Ring closure check: c1 (carboxamide carbon) … n n2 CC c3 cc(...)ccc3 N c12. The final atom c12 closes ring 1 to the carboxamide carbon and ring 2 to the n2 nitrogen. This works because the c bonded to N (the NH-bearing carbon) is bonded to the carboxamide carbon and to the ring nitrogen. In the drawing, that carbon is bonded to NH, to the carboxamide-bearing carbon, and to N1, so the connectivity matches.

The benzo ring: c3 (bearing CH2), c (H), c(C=O), c, c, c3(N). The CH2-bearing carbon is adjacent to a CH, which is adjacent to the carbonyl carbon, matching the drawing.

The isoindoline attachment: c1ccc2C(=O)N...C(=O)c2c1 places the piperidine N on the aromatic carbon c1, which is adjacent to the CH next to the ring-fusion carbon, giving position 5. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: NC(=O)c1c(-c2ccc(Oc3ccccc3)cc2)nn2CCc3cc(ccc3Nc12)C(=O)N1CCN(CC1)CC1CCN(CC1)c1ccc2C(=O)N(C3CCC(=O)NC3=O)C(=O)c2c1

name: rb_0203
text:
I read the drawing as a 1-ring macrocycle built from these pieces, then wrote the SMILES from them.

- **Ornithine unit:** the side chain is CH2CH2CH2NH-Boc. Its α-carbon carries a ring secondary amine (NH–CH2 to the pyridine) and a C(=O) that forms an amide to the next residue.
- **Diaminobutyric acid unit:** the side chain is CH2CH2NH-Boc. Its α-carbon is bonded to the amide NH on one side and to C(=O)–N(CH3) on the other.
- **N-methyl tryptophan unit:** the α-carbon carries CH2 to the indole C3, and the indole nitrogen bears a Boc group. Its C(=O) forms an amide to NH–CH2 on the benzene ring.
- **Benzene ring:** the substituents run CH2N, then Br, two CH, then Cl, then S. Both the Br and the S are ortho to the CH2N carbon.
- **Pyridine ring:** C3 carries the CH2N, and C2 carries the S, which bridges to the benzene ring. The ring nitrogen is adjacent to C2.

All three wedged α-carbons work out to S, which is consistent with L-amino acids. I assigned each from the wedge direction and CIP priorities (N > C=O > side-chain CH2 > H, with H pointing away from the viewer), then mapped that onto the SMILES neighbour order.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)OC(=O)NCCC[C@H]1C(=O)N[C@@H](CCNC(=O)OC(C)(C)C)C(=O)N(C)[C@@H](Cc2cn(C(=O)OC(C)(C)C)c3ccccc23)C(=O)NCc4c(Br)ccc(Cl)c4Sc5ncccc5CN1

name: rb_0208
text:
I read the structure region by region and assembled the SMILES below.

**Left part.** A pyrazolo[1,5-a][1,5]benzodiazepine core. The pyrazole carries a carboxamide (C(N)=O) at C3 and a 4-phenoxyphenyl group at C2. The pyrazole N1 is bonded to a CH2CH2 chain that leads to the benzo ring. The other pyrazole carbon is bonded to an NH, which is bonded to the benzo ring. The benzo ring carries the C(=O) group that links to the piperidine nitrogen.

**Linker.** The piperidine is substituted at C4 with a CH2 that connects to a piperazine nitrogen. The other piperazine nitrogen is attached to the isoindoline-dione aryl ring.

- N3

I checked the isoquinoline fragment Nc3ccc4c(ccnc4-Ar)c3. The atoms are c3 (C6), c (C7), c (C8), c4 (C8a), then c(...) which is C4a with branch ccn, followed by c4. That is wrong, so I rewrote it.

name: rb_0235
text:
This structure looks like a FAPI-type conjugate: a (4,4-difluoro-2-cyanopyrrolidinyl)glycyl amide on a quinoline-4-carboxamide, linked through an 8-amino succinamide and an ethylenediamine to a DOTA-glutamic acid unit (DOTA-GA).

**Left fragment.** The pyrrolidine nitrogen is acylated by C(=O)CH2NH. C2 carries the nitrile, C3 is CH2, C4 is CF2, and C5 is CH2 bonded to N. The C2 stereocentre is drawn with a bold wedge to the CN group. I wrote it as N#C[C@@H]1CC(F)(F)CN1C(=O)CNC(=O)... and checked the chirality below.

**Chirality at C2.** Its neighbours are CN, N (ring), CH2 (ring C3) and H. In the drawing C2 sits at about (95, 200), with the CN above at (75, 125) on the wedge, N to the right at (140, 225), and C3 to the lower left at (40, 235). H is implied and points away from the viewer.

In the SMILES `N#C[C@@H]1CC(F)(F)CN1...`, the neighbour order at C2 is CN (preceding atom), H, ring-closure 1 (which is N), then C3. For `@@`, looking from the first neighbour (CN), the remaining neighbours H, N, C3 run clockwise.

Check against the drawing, viewed from the front: the wedged CN is toward the viewer, and the other three are N (right), C3 (lower left) and H (back). Viewed from the front with H behind, the priorities are N > CN > C3 (CN has N,N,N; C3 has C,H,H). Going N (right, lower) → CN (up) → C3 (lower left) runs counterclockwise on screen, which gives S with H at the back. This is the usual (S)-2-cyanopyrrolidine, as expected for FAPI compounds.

For the SMILES, the chirality at `[C@@H]` with neighbours in the order CN, H, N, C3 must be converted to CIP. With H as the second neighbour, `@@` from CN means H, N, C3 are clockwise. Swapping to put H first gives the order H, CN, N, C3, which is one swap and so `@`. Looking from H, CN → N → C3 is then counterclockwise. Viewed from the side opposite H, it is clockwise: CN → N → C3. The priority order N → CN → C3 is an odd permutation of that, so it is counterclockwise, giving S. This matches the drawing.

**Quinoline.** The 4-carboxamide is C(=O)NH on C4, and the ring nitrogen is N1. C8 carries NH-C(=O)CH2CH2C(=O)NH-CH2CH2-NH-C(=O)CH2CH2-CH(COOH)-N(cyclen).

**Cyclen.** The ring N atoms are: N1 bearing the CH(COOH) substituent, and three N-CH2COOH groups.

- The CH2CH2–O–CH2 chain runs to the central benzene ring.

**Central benzene ring.** It carries three substituents:

**Benzimidazole.**

name: rb_0255
text:
This is a PROTAC-like molecule. I read it in three parts: the pomalidomide end, the linker, and the isoquinoline/pyrazolotriazine end.

**Pomalidomide end.** The isoindoline-1,3-dione carries an NH at the 4-position of the benzene ring. The imide nitrogen is attached to a piperidine-2,6-dione at its 3-position. This part is: O=C1CCC(N2C(=O)c3cccc(NCC(=O)...)c3C2=O)C(=O)N1.

**Linker.** From the aryl NH the chain runs: NH–CH2–C(=O)–NH–CH2CH2–O–CH2CH2–N(CH3)–CH2–CH=CH–C(=O)–NH–. The double bond is drawn trans (E). The final NH is attached to the isoquinoline at C6.

**Isoquinoline.** The ring system has C1 bearing the aryl group and N2 next to it. The fused benzo ring carries the amide NH at C6. Written from the amide: c1cc2c(cc1)c(-aryl)nccc2. In the image, C1 is attached to the phenyl and N lies below it. The amide-bearing carbon is on the upper-left of the benzo ring, adjacent to C5, which is attached to C4a. I wrote this as c1(NC(=O)...)ccc2c(c1)ccnc2-Ar, checking the ring positions:
- Atoms: c1 (C6), c (C7), c (C8), c2 (C8a), c(c1) (C5, closing to C6 through c1), then C4a is the same atom as c2's partner.
- This SMILES is not quite right, so I rewrote it as c1(N...)ccc2c(c1)ccnc2Ar. The atoms are C6, C7, C8, C8a (c2), C4a (c(c1)), then ccn gives C4, C3, N2, and c2 is C1 closing to C8a.
- Here the c(c1) atom is bonded to C5, which closes the ring to C6. That requires an extra atom. Correct is c1(N)ccc2c(c1)ccnc2: C6, C7, C8, C8a, C4a (with branch c1 = C5 closing to C6), then C4, C3, N, C1. C1 closes to C8a, so C1 is attached to C8a, which is correct.

**Aryl and pyrazolotriazine end.** The phenyl is ortho-substituted with CH2NH–. The NH is attached to the triazine carbon (C4) of a pyrazolo[1,5-a][1,3,5]triazine. The triazine C2 carries a 4-aminopiperidin-1-yl group. The pyrazole carbon C8 carries an isopropyl group.

Pyrazolotriazine SMILES: c1(NCAr)nc(N2CCC(N)CC2)nc3c(C(C)C)cnn13.

Full SMILES:
O=C1CCC(N2C(=O)c3cccc(NCC(=O)NCCOCCN(C)C/C=C/C(=O)Nc4ccc5c(c4)ccnc5-c4ccccc4CNc4nc(N5CCC(N)CC5)nc5c(C(C)C)cnn45)c3C2=O)C(=O)N1

name: rb_0258
text:
I read the structure region by region and assembled the SMILES below.

**Left fragment.** A 6-methylpyridin-2-yl group is bonded through NH to a C(=O). That carbonyl sits on a benzene ring carrying a methyl ortho to it and a fluorine on the next carbon. The ring carbon after the fluorine bears the pyrazole.

**Benzene ring SMILES.** Ring atoms: c1 (C=O attached), c(C) (methyl), c(F), c (attached to the pyrazole), c, c. Written out: C(=O)c1ccc(c(F)c1C)-c2...

**Tricyclic core.** The pyrazole is c2nn3CCc4cc(...)ccc4Nc3c2C(N)=O.
- The pyrazole carbon bearing the aryl group (C2) is bonded to N, which is bonded to N3.
- N3 carries the CH2CH2 chain, which leads to the benzo ring.
- The benzo ring is closed through NH to the pyrazole carbon C3a, which is bonded to C3 bearing the carboxamide.
- The piperazine sits on the benzo ring carbon meta to the CH2 attachment (the carbon para to the NH-bearing ring carbon is not the one used).

**Benzo ring check.** The ring runs CH2-attached carbon, then CH, then C(piperazine), then CH, CH, and C-NH. The drawing shows the piperazine-bearing carbon adjacent to the CH that neighbors the CH2-bearing carbon, so the ring is c4cc(N...)ccc4N.

**Right fragment.** The piperazine N' is attached to azetidine C3. That azetidine's N is bonded to the C3 of a second azetidine, whose N is bonded to the isoindoline-1,3-dione aromatic ring. The isoindoline N is attached to a piperidine-2,6-dione carbon, and the imide N carries SEM, CH2OCH2CH2Si(CH3)3.

**Isoindoline aromatic ring.** The azetidine N sits at position 5, giving c1ccc2c(c1)C(=O)N(...)C2=O.

**Full SMILES.**
Cc1cccc(NC(=O)c2ccc(c(F)c2C)-c2nn3CCc4cc(ccc4Nc3c2C(N)=O)N2CCN(CC2)C2CN(C2)C2CN(C2)c2ccc3C(=O)N(C4CCC(=O)N(COCC[Si](C)(C)C)C4=O)C(=O)c3c2)n1

**Ring-closure check.** In the core, "c2nn3CCc4cc(...)ccc4Nc3c2C(N)=O" uses ring label 2 for the pyrazole, and the later reuse of 2 inside the branch is legitimate only if label 2 is closed first. Label 2 is closed at "c2C(N)=O" at the end of the core, but the branch containing N2CCN(CC2) appears before that closure. This would clash, so I renumbered the labels in the piperazine and the later rings.

Final: Cc1cccc(NC(=O)c2ccc(c(F)c2C)-c2nn3CCc4cc(ccc4Nc3c2C(N)=O)N5CCN(CC5)C6CN(C6)C7CN(C7)c8ccc9C(=O)N(C%10CCC(=O)N(COCC[Si](C)(C)C)C%10=O)C(=O)c9c8)n1

name: rb_0259
text:
I read the molecule as a macrocycle built from a 2,3-disubstituted pyridine, a 2,3,4,6-substituted benzene joined by a thioether, and three amino-acid residues. The SMILES is written starting from the pyridine ring.

**Fragments read from the drawing**
- **Pyridine:** C2 carries the S bridge and C3 carries a CH2–NH group.
- **Benzene ring:** one carbon bears S, the adjacent carbon bears the CH2–NH group, and the next carbon bears Br. The other carbon next to the S-bearing one bears Cl.
- **Dab residue:** the α-carbon is bonded to the ring-side NH and to a C(=O). Its side chain is CH2CH2NH–C(=O)C(CH3)3, a pivaloyl amide.
- **Orn(Boc) residue:** the side chain is (CH2)3NH–C(=O)OC(CH3)3, and the α-carbon carries an NH and a C(=O) that connects to the N-methyl amide.
- **Trp(Boc) residue:** the nitrogen is N-methylated, the side chain is CH2 to indol-3-yl, and the indole N carries a Boc group. The C(=O) of this residue is bonded to NH–CH2 on the benzene ring.

**Stereochemistry**
Each of the three α-carbons has a wedge on its side-chain bond, which puts the implicit H at the back. Tracing the three drawn neighbours of each centre gives a clockwise N → side chain → C(=O) sequence, which corresponds to `@@` in the SMILES order N, H, side chain, C(=O). All three centres therefore take `@@`.

SMILES: c1cnc2c(c1)CN[C@@H](CCNC(=O)C(C)(C)C)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCNC(=O)OC(C)(C)C)C(=O)N(C)[C@@H](Cc1cn(C(=O)OC(C)(C)C)c3ccccc13)C(=O)NCc1c(Br)ccc(Cl)c1S2

name: rb_0257
text:
I read the structure in regions and assembled the SMILES from them.

- **Macrocycle:** a cyclen (12-membered ring with four nitrogens) in which every nitrogen carries a CH2C(=O)NH2 group. One ring carbon, between two adjacent nitrogens, bears a CH2–C6H4 (p-phenylene) group.
- **Thiourea link:** the para position of that benzene ring carries NH–C(=S)–NH, which connects through (CH2)4 to the ε-carbon of the central lysine.
- **Central lysine:** its α-NH is acylated by a C(=O)CH2CH2 unit followed by a triethylene-glycol-type chain, with three ether oxygens and a terminal NH. That NH is acylated by C(=O)CH2–O, which is attached to the quinoline at C7.
- **Second lysine:** the central lysine's C(=O) forms an amide with the α-NH of a second lysine, which has a free CO2H. Its ε-NH is acylated by (4-iodophenyl)acetyl.
- **Quinoline end:** the quinoline C4 carries C(=O)NH–CH2–C(=O)–N linked to a pyrrolidine whose C2 bears B(OH)2.
- **Stereochemistry:**
  - Both lysine α-carbons are drawn with wedges and work out as S, the L configuration.
  - The boroproline carbon is drawn with a hashed bond to boron and works out as R. That is the same spatial arrangement as L-proline, because boron ranks below the ring carbon in priority.
  - The ring carbon of the cyclen is drawn with plain bonds, so it gets no stereo label.

I wrote the SMILES with these pieces joined in that order and checked ring closures and atom counts against the drawing.

text:
I read the molecule as a PROTAC-type structure: a VHL ligand joined through an octanedioyl linker to a pyridine-piperidine fragment. I wrote the SMILES from the thiazole end, working along the structure.

- **Hydroxyproline:** the pyrrolidine has a 4-OH and a 2-carboxamide. I took the (2S,4R) configuration from the wedges and hashes.
- **tert-Leucine:** the N-acylated tert-leucine (CH bearing a tert-butyl group) is attached to the pyrrolidine nitrogen through its carbonyl. I took the S configuration from the wedge.
- **Linker:** an octanedioyl chain, counted as 8 carbons with 6 CH2 groups between the two C=O groups. One end is an amide to the tert-leucine NH. The other end is an amide to the piperidine nitrogen.
- **Piperidine and pyridine:** the piperidine is attached at its 4-position to C4 of a pyridine. Pyridine C2 carries an NH–pyrazin-2-yl group. Pyridine C6 carries a 3,3-difluoropyrrolidin-1-yl group.
