name: rb_0260
text:
I read this as a symmetric dimer: two identical bicyclic pyrrolo-fused diazocinone units joined through a benzene-1,3-disulfonyl linker.

Each half is built as follows:
- **Ring core:** A proline-derived pyrrolidine is fused through its nitrogen and its adjacent ring-fusion carbon to an eight-membered ring. The eight-membered ring contains the ring-fusion CH, two CH2 groups, a sulfonamide nitrogen, a CH2, an amino-bearing CH, and the lactam C=O on the pyrrolidine nitrogen.
- **Pyrrolidine substituent:** The pyrrolidine carbon next to the nitrogen carries a C(=O)NH–CH(Ph)2 (benzhydryl amide).
- **Amino side chain:** The amino-bearing CH carries NH–C(=O)–CH(CH3)–NH–CH3, an N-methylalanine amide.
- **Linker:** The sulfonamide nitrogen of each half is bonded to one SO2 group of the central benzene ring, with the two SO2 groups meta to each other.

The right half is a mirror reflection of the left in the drawing, with wedge and hash bonds swapped. I therefore treated the two halves as having the same configuration at each centre and wrote them with equivalent CIP descriptors.

I could not read every wedge and hash with certainty, so the stereodescriptors are partly assumed. I used the natural-type configuration: S at the alanine carbon, the amino-bearing carbon, the proline-type carbon and the ring-fusion carbon.

The SMILES below is valid and accounts for every atom in the drawing.

text:
Reading the structure region by region:

- **Pyrazine:** the ring has a methyl on one carbon and N atoms at the positions shown. The ring is c1(C)cnc(N...)cn1, so the methyl carbon is adjacent to a ring N and the NH-bearing carbon is adjacent to the other N. The NH links the pyrazine to the pyridine.
- **Pyridine:** the ring N sits between C2 (bearing the NH–pyrazine) and C6 (bearing the difluoropyrrolidine). C4 carries the piperidin-4-yl group, and C3 and C5 are CH.
- **Difluoropyrrolidine:** N-linked pyrrolidine with CF2 at the 3-position.
- **Piperidine:** N-acylated with C(=O)CH2–O–Ar.
- **Isoindoline-1,3-dione:** the aryl ether is on C4 of the isoindoline-1,3-dione. Its N bears the 2,6-dioxopiperidin-3-yl group, drawn with no stereochemistry.

Checking the pyrazine: c1(C) is bonded to c (CH), then n, then c(N), then c (CH), then n1 closing back to c1(C). The methyl carbon therefore has ring N neighbors on one side and CH on the other. In the drawing, the methyl carbon at the top connects to CH (top) and to a ring C=N on the left, which matches.

Checking the pyridine: c2 (NH-bearing) – cc(piperidinyl) – c – c(pyrrolidinyl) – n2. In the SMILES, c2cc(...)cc(n2)N2... gives c2, c, c(pip), c, c(N-pyrrolidine) with n2 closing the ring. This is correct.

name: rb_0266
text:
I read the structure in four pieces and joined them into one SMILES.

- **Right-hand end:** a benzothiazole carrying a 2-hydroxypropan-2-yl group at C5 and an NH–C(=O)–(6-trifluoromethylpyridin-2-yl) amide at C6. Its C2 is bonded to a 1,4-disubstituted cyclohexane.
- **Cyclohexane:** the wedge to the benzothiazole and the hashed CH2 on the opposite carbon indicate a trans arrangement. I wrote this as `[C@H]1CC[C@@H](...)CC1`, which I recalled as the trans pattern (as in trans-4-methylcyclohexanol) rather than deriving it from the drawing.
- **Centre:** the cyclohexyl CH2 is bonded to the N of a 2-azaspiro[3.3]heptane, and the cyclobutane CH of that spirocycle carries the central CH. That CH bears two arms:
  - a CH2–NH arm leading to a 4-amino-isoindoline-1,3-dione whose ring N is attached to a 2,6-dioxopiperidin-3-yl group (the thalidomide-type end);
  - a CH2–N arm leading to a piperidine whose C4 is bonded to a phenyl ring.

text:
I read this as a silicon-rhodamine (Si-rhodamine) dye carrying a diaza-crown ether (a 1,4-dioxa-7,10-diazacyclododecane ring, a calcium/metal-sensing motif) on its pendant benzoate ring.

**Xanthene core.** The top ring carries NMe2 and is bonded to Si(Me)2. The bottom-right ring carries the =N+(Me)2 iminium. The central carbon (C9) joins the two rings and bears the pendant aryl group.

**Pendant benzoate ring.** Going around the ring from the carbon attached to C9:
- C1 is attached to the xanthene C9.
- C2 bears the carboxylate (C(=O)[O-]).
- C3 is an aromatic CH.
- C4 bears OMe.
- C5 bears the crown-ether nitrogen.
- C6 is an aromatic CH, which closes back to C1.

**Crown ring.** The ring is N–CH2CH2–O–CH2CH2–N–CH2CH2–O–CH2CH2 back to the first N, which is 12 atoms in total. One N is attached to the benzoate ring. The other N is attached to a 2-methoxyphenyl group.

**SMILES construction.**
- Xanthene part: CN(C)c1ccc2c(c1)[Si](C)(C)c1cc(=[N+](C)C)ccc1C2=... Here the central carbon is double-bonded to the ring so that the iminium ring is quinoid. Written out, the iminium ring is C2=C1C=CC(=[N+](C)C)C=C1[Si].
- Full SMILES: CN(C)c1ccc2c(c1)[Si](C)(C)C1=CC(=[N+](C)C)C=CC1=C2c1cc(N2CCOCCN(CCOCC2)c2ccccc2OC)c(OC)cc1C(=O)[O-]

**Check on the iminium ring.** C1(=CC(=[N+](C)C)C=CC1=C2…) has Si–C1, then C1=C, then C(=N+), then C=C, then C1(=C2). The ring atoms are C1, CH, C(=N), CH, CH, C(=C9), which is 6 atoms. C1 has a double bond to CH and a single bond to Si. C(=N) is attached to CH, which is double-bonded to CH in "C=C", and that CH is attached to the final ring carbon, which carries the exocyclic double bond to C9. The ring is therefore conjugated correctly.

**Check on the crown ring.** N2CCOCCN(...)CCOCC2 gives N, C, C, O, C, C, N, C, C, O, C, C and back to the first N, which is 12 atoms. The ring-closure digit 2 is reused after the xanthene ring 2 has already closed, which is valid.

text:

- The adjacent quinone ring has the amide NH, a C=O and an aromatic OH.
- The aromatic ring carries a methyl and the furanone oxygen, and it is fused to the furanone ring, which bears a C=O.

- For centres with an implicit H, I took H to point opposite the drawn wedge or hash.

text:

name: rb_0350
text:
Reading the drawing region by region gave this structure:

- **Left ring:** a 3-fluoro-pyridin-4-one whose nitrogen is bonded to a benzene ring (ring A).
- **Ring A:** two adjacent substituents sit ortho to each other. One is a CH2–O link to the pyridine; the other is a three-carbon chain (CH2CH2CH2) running to an ether oxygen on the central benzene.
- **Central benzene (ring B):** it carries three groups.
  - The propyl-chain ether oxygen.
  - The pyridine ring, attached at the position meta to that oxygen.
  - A CH2 group to the benzimidazole, ortho to the oxygen.
- **Pyridine:** it is 2,6-disubstituted, with ring B at one position and the O–CH2 link to ring A at the other. These links close the macrocycle.
- **Benzimidazole:** C2 bears the CH2 group. N1 bears a CH2–oxetan-2-yl group, and the carboxylic acid sits on the carbon one position away from the ring-fusion carbon next to N1 (position 6).
- **Stereochemistry:** the only drawn stereocentre is the oxetane C2, with a hashed bond to the CH2N group, so the H points toward the viewer. The priorities are O > CH2N > ring CH2 > H. Viewed from the front the O → CH2N → ring CH2 sequence runs clockwise. Because H faces the viewer, the true configuration is the reverse, which is S. In the SMILES below, `[C@@H]` with the O ring closure listed first encodes S.

**Chromophore**

- A phenoxazine unit is fused onto the core. It has a C=N, a ring oxygen and a benzene ring, and the benzene ring has an O-piperidin-4-yl group.

- The quinone-ring carbon next to the C=O carries the amide NH.

- Next comes CH=CH (trans), then CH=C(CH3) (cis, as drawn), then the amide C(=O)–NH.

**Stereochemistry**
- I read each stereocentre from its wedge or hash and the neighbouring bond directions.
- I cross-checked the chain centres against the known rifamycin/rifampicin configuration, and they agreed.
- The E/Z geometry of the three C=C bonds comes from the drawing.
